analysis.title: Midterms Unlikely a 'Clearing Event'
key_insights: Since 1962, the SPX has averaged a -13.76% drawdown at some point in the June-December window of midterm election years. This year the SPX has seen only a -4.5% drawdown after June 1st, which would be the second-smallest since 1962 (only 2006 was smaller at -3.6%).

Midterms are often a 'clearing event' with a strong November because the SPX is typically weak into the elections. BTIG says this year's setup is the opposite, and the SPX also moved inversely to the average pattern in February/March. Consensus expects a post-midterm rally. BTIG thinks the opposite is more likely.

The SPX 200 DMA is in play. Small-caps, mid-caps, transports, semiconductors and many sectors have tested their 200 DMAs. BTIG suspects the SPX is next, which would bring it toward 7300 at a minimum. That area is also the summer lows, so an overshoot of the 200 DMA would not be surprising, as in March.
33% of days in 2026 have seen price and breadth move in opposite directions. BTIG says history suggests this is unlikely to continue much longer.
Put/Call ratios remain well below levels seen in March and July of this year. BTIG says it is hard to think a meaningful low is in when there is a lack of hedging.

B vs. CCC junk spreads have reached 7.8% or more only five times since 1996. In the four prior occurrences the SPX was at least -11.8% from its 52-week high, and twice it was already in a -30% drawdown. The current SPX drawdown is about -2%, which BTIG says suggests downside risk for stocks.

Semis failed the bounce off support. The 200 DMA is holding for SOXX and SMH, but the equal-weight XSD has already lost its 200 DMA. BTIG continues to think semis work lower over the coming weeks and months.
Tech credit continues to deteriorate. Hyper Scaler CDS continues to widen, and IG Tech CDS is the widest since 2022 while the S&P 500 Tech sector is only a few percent below highs.
Private credit cannot rally. BDCs are at fresh multi-year lows, unable to sustain a rally, and have diverged meaningfully from software.
Equal-weight software (XSW) is breaking out of a two-year range with relative strength at YTD highs. BTIG calls it the place to look for momentum. XSW vs. XSD is breaking out of a one-year base.
Other vulnerable groups flagged: industrials (losing support), healthcare, restaurants (CMG back to 2022 levels), airlines (struggling) and casinos (back to March lows).

Junk credit spreads are widening while the SPX drawdown is only about -2%, a combination that has not occurred in prior episodes.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus expects a post-midterm rally, because midterm years usually see the SPX weak into the elections and strong in November.
tension_points.bear_case: This year the SPX is not weak into the elections (only a -4.5% drawdown since June 1st), junk spreads are blowing out, hedging is light, and the 200 DMA is likely to be tested, so a clearing event is unlikely.

theme_stances.key_argument: The SPX was not weak into the midterms this year, so the usual post-election rally setup is absent and the opposite is more likely.
theme_stances.evidence: while consensus is that we see a post mid-term rally, we think the opposite

theme_stances.key_argument: B vs. CCC spreads at 7.8% or more have historically come with much deeper SPX drawdowns than the current -2%.
theme_stances.evidence: either "it's different this time", or SPX is likely in for some rough sledding
